case.summary: The case was opened after a portfolio sweep flagged four online purchases of $400–$500 each on card C05423-K1 within 30 minutes, totaling $1,884.76. Investigation found the amounts were far outside the card’s history, matched a known under-$500 run shape seen on 11 other cards, and linked to a coordinated scheme. The fraud probability was 0.99 and the case was escalated to a fraud analyst. The analyst confirmed the pattern and agreed it was a coordinated fraud scheme. The card was blocked, pending authorizations were declined, connected cards were monitored, a report was filed, and the case was escalated to an analyst. The case remains open for further review.

sar.narrative: The suspicious activity involved card C05423-K1 and customer C05423. On 2016-12-03 at 12:00, 12:06, 12:22, and 12:30, four online transactions (IDs 3509526, 3509535, 3509563, 3509576) each between $400 and $500 were authorized, totaling $1,884.76. The amounts were far above the card’s historical average of $43.72 and just under a $500 authorization threshold, indicating structuring. The same under-$500 run shape appeared on 11 other cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06881-K1, C07297-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2) within ±30 days, showing a coordinated scheme. Device profiles linked to the card were known and matched the activity, supporting the fraud hypothesis. The exposure amount of $1,884.76 is below the $2,500 threshold but exceeds $1,000, triggering a report. The case was escalated to a fraud analyst, who confirmed the pattern and coordinated the actions. The card was blocked, pending authorizations were declined, connected cards were monitored, and a report was filed. The investigation remains open for further monitoring of the linked cards.
